subject: Request: Anchored price ceiling + renewal protection for AcuteHealth multi-year
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Anchored price ceiling + renewal protection for AcuteHealth multi-year

Team — looping you in for urgent deal-desk exec approval. AcuteHealth is asking for a 3-year committed package (annual billing) for their core inference usage. Key ask: a locked per-token rate for 36 months with an uplift cap on any annual increases and a renewal protection clause that limits renewal increases (if they renew) to a fixed band.

High-level terms requested by customer (from procurement):
- Term: 36 months (annual invoicing)
- Effective ARR: $2,700,000 year 1 run-rate
- Upfront discount: 28% off list for year 1
- Price lock: no per-token price increases for 36 months (absolute lock)
- Renewal protection: at renewal, any increase <= 8% annually (cap) and an uplift cap of 6% year-over-year during contract term if we offer optional add-ons

Why we should consider:
- Very strong reference in healthcare (HIT integrations)
- High sustained utilization; predictable workload profile that maps well to Redwood Dedicated pools
- Competitor risk: they've spoken with two vendors who will not commit to price locks this long

We need an exec sign-off on two exceptions:
1) Absolute 36-month price lock (no market-driven per-token adjustments) — this is outside standard guardrails.
2) 28% submerged discount + renewal protection cap (limits our ability to recover inflation at renewals).

Attachments: pricing_model_ACUTE-4571.xlsx (breakdown), draft_msa_ACUTE-4571.pdf (redlines), comps_summary_Q2.xlsx (market comps).

Requesting: approval or counter guidance by EOD 2028-07-15 so we can return a clean response to Emily.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Anchored price ceiling + renewal protection for AcuteHealth multi-year

Marcus —
Appreciate the context. A few quick notes from deal desk perspective:
- 28% year 1 is near upper bound for a 3-year commitment at this ARR; we usually require a firm capacity commitment for a discount this steep. Do they want Reserved / Dedicated capacity? If so, that makes the economics more palatable.
- Absolute 36-month lock is the larger policy exception. We typically allow a hard lock for 12–24 months and then an indexed floor.
- Renewal protection (<=8% cap) is reasonable as a goodwill item but should be coupled with step-up triggers tied to utilization or model upgrades (i.e., if they expand usage >40% we have negotiated repricing).

If you can confirm: Dedicated pool commitment? Any compliance asks (SOC2 artifacts)? I'll draft the Executive Approval memo once we nail the operational mitigations.

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Deal Desk
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Anchored price ceiling + renewal protection for AcuteHealth multi-year

Marcus — quick data from finance after reviewing the spreadsheet:
- Modeled NPV delta vs standard list (3-year): -12.4% (net to Redwood) given 28% year1 + price lock.
- If we require Dedicated pool reservation covering 85% of their peak qps, the delta moves to -5.8% (acceptable with an SLA addendum).
- Cashflow: annual invoicing improves our cash profile vs monthly; recommend annual prepayment option for further protection (convertible to a 3% increase in effective price if they prepay annually).

Proposed commercial guardrails to present to customer if we proceed:
1) Price lock limited to per-token list rate for baseline usage up to committed qps; overage charges billed at current list with a 12% premium (discourages unbounded expansion).
2) Require Dedicated reservation covering 85% of committed baseline; if they decline, reduce lock to 18 months and adjust discount to 20% year1.
3) Renewal protection cap of 8% but with a utilization-triggered repricing clause (if usage growth >40% year-over-year we reserve right to renegotiate uplift).

I'll attach a redlined clause set for legal to reference.

-Monica
Head of Finance Ops
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-16T14:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Anchored price ceiling + renewal protection for AcuteHealth multi-year

Marcus / Team —
After legal review (see inline notes in draft_msa), I'm comfortable escalating the following for exec approval:
- Approve price lock for 36 months on baseline committed capacity only (as Monica suggested) — this addresses the exposure.
- Approve up to 30% discount year 1 provided we secure the Dedicated reservation and an annual prepay option (3% price benefit if they prepay).
- Approve renewal protection cap of 8% with the explicit utilization-trigger override (language to be added to MSA Section 5.3).

Risks called out in legal redlines: data residency addendum and audit rights wording — procurement will expect SOC2 evidence. We'll share SOC2 report via the gated portal; no special exceptions needed.

Recommend we escalate to execs for sign-off on the two items below: 
1) Exception: 36-month baseline price lock (conditional on Dedicated reservation covering >=85% baseline).
2) Exception: one-time commercial approval for 28% year1 discount (we can offer up to 30% with annual prepay).

If approved, I'll finalize MSA language and send to Emily.

-Ben
VP Legal (acting)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Finalizing exec note for Sarah/Finance/CEO escalation (copy below) and will include your guardrails.

--- Exec note (for approval) ---
From: Marcus Lin, Director, Strategic Accounts
To: Sarah Bennett (CRO), David Kim (CFO), Markus Klein (CEO)
Date: 2028-07-17
Subject: Approval requested: Exceptions for AcuteHealth (ACUTE-4571) — 36-month baseline price lock + renewal protection & up to 30% year1 discount

Summary:
AcuteHealth proposes a 3-year committed engagement at ~$2.7M ARR (year1). They're requesting a 36-month absolute per-token price lock, an initial discount in the high 20s (they asked for 28%), and renewal protection limiting increases to 8% annually.

Recommended approval (conditional):
- Approve baseline price lock for 36 months ONLY for committed Dedicated reservation covering >=85% of baseline usage.
- Approve up to 30% discount in year 1 if customer signs annual prepay (3% adder to effective price if prepaid) and commits to Dedicated reservation.
- Approve renewal protection cap of 8% subject to utilization-triggered repricing (>40% YoY growth).

Rationale:
- Strategic healthcare reference; predictable workload and high retention probability.
- Economics acceptable with Dedicated reservation and prepay.
- Competitive win that materially expands our footprint in healthcare integrations.

If approved, legal will finalize MSA redlines and operations will lock the Dedicated pool sizing.

Requested: Exec sign-off or escalated guidance by 2028-07-18 EOD to meet procurement timeline.

--- end exec note ---

Marissa / Monica / Ben — please let me know if you want additional numbers in the packet. I'll send to Sarah and David once I have sign-off from each of you.

Thanks,
Marcus
